column1: # boru Language Specification: edge-quote-4 — code-as-data in data context
# Edge cases for the remaining code-as-data surfaces: ParenExpr in
# data context (map values evaluate inline at BIND time — an early
# quotes, escapes, atoms), and the implicit-quote boundary probed
# from inside (for-body `i` visibility and shadowing, each bodies
# reaching outer defs, held lists driving higher-order words).
# Expected values use the canon renderer. See eng/go/parser notes in
# --- §1 ParenExpr in map values: inline eval at bind ---------------------

column3: a paren map value evaluates inline
sibling paren values evaluate independently
nested map, nested paren
infix-form arithmetic inside a data slot
a paren value reads live bindings at bind time
…and may call user fns
parens nest inside the value expression
a paren inside a LIST evaluates during list eval
a quoted name rides a list as an atom
paren grouping composes at top level too

column1: # --- §2 the early snapshot: bind-time, not read-time ---------------------
def c 1 def m {a:(c add 1)} def c 10 m
column3: rebinding c does NOT change the snapshot

column1: def c 2 def m {a:(c mul 5)} undef c m
column3: the snapshot survives undef of its source

column1: def c 1 def m {a:(c add 1)} def c 10 {a:(c add 1)}
column3: a NEW map literal snapshots the NEW binding

column1: def c 1 def m {a:(c add 1), b:c} def c 9 m
column3: bare-word fields snapshot exactly like paren fields

column1: def c 1 def xs [c add 1] def c 10 xs
column3: def of a list body is the same early snapshot

column1: def c 1 def xs [quote [c add 1]] def c 10 do (xs get 0)
column3: …but HELD code re-resolves when finally run — late binding via quote

column1: def c 1 def w word [c] def c 10 w
column3: …and a word splice is late too: the splice re-reads at reference
a backtick literal with no holes is a plain string
a hole runs code and interpolates the result
adjacent holes concatenate their renderings
a template is ALWAYS a String, even when one hole is the whole body
…pinned by typeof: the non-empty string subtype
double quotes are plain characters inside a template
holes read live bindings
an atom interpolates as its bare name
two atom holes, two bare names
none interpolates as lowercase none
a type literal interpolates as its name
templates NEST — the inner template is a hole's expression
…to any depth
a template evaluates inside a list literal
the \n escape stays one string (canon shows the escape)
an escaped backtick is a literal character
the \$ escape suppresses interpolation — ${ becomes text
an ordinary quoted string never interpolates
a hole is a full sub-program — quotation works inside it
integer division renders its integer
independent holes: one computes, one counts held code
the loop index i IS visible inside the body
a range form starts i at the lower bound
a stepped range steps i
i is an ordinary operand inside the body
the body i SHADOWS an outer i binding
…and the outer binding is intact after the loop
i does not leak out of a loop that never bound it outside
sequential loops each rebind i from zero
…and /q beats the binding: the NAME rides out as an atom
the body mixes i with an outer binding

column1: def square fn [[x:Integer][Integer][x mul x]] [1 2 3] each [square]
column3: an each body calls an outer fn by name
an each body reads an outer value binding
…and maps one result per element
iota feeds each — the body sees each element
an each inside a fn body resolves at call time
a branch may hold code of its own — still held after the branch runs
…bind the branch result and the held size reads through
a branch may run held code of its own via do
a HELD data list is still a real List for each
do over held plain data just replays the elements
a hole is real code — unknown words are errors
a paren map value is real code too
an each body's unknown word errors when the body runs
quote inside a paren value stores the atom
a held list stores in a map field without evaluating
…and runs later straight off the field read
